To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. Bacterial RNA polymerases can initiate transcription with NAD+, FAD and UDP-Glc, but not with other nucleotides; 2. NAD+ and FAD stimulate promoter escape, but UDP-Glc does not; 3. The efficiency of initiation with Nucleotides depends on the Rifampicinicin-binding pocket of β subunit;
1) Bacterial RNA polymerases are able to cap RNA with various cofactor and cell wall precusors.

bacterial RNA polymerase is capable of using various cofactors and highly abundant cell wall precursors to initiate transcription in vivo, and that this ability is affected by Rifampicin-resistance and σ subunit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
bacterial RNA polymerase and its role in the cell wall biosynthesis.
bacterial transcription and its regulation.
the initiation of transcription by RNA polymerase and with the mechanism of promoter escape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial transcription is initiated by NAD+, and that the other cofactors, FAD, UDP-Glucosamine, UDP-Gluctose and UDP-MurNAcpentapeptide are not used to initiate transcription.
RNA polymerase is not able to cap RNA with NAD+ in vivo, and that the observed NAD+-initiated transcription in vitro is a result of a non-specific binding of the cofactor to the enzyme.
RNA polymerase is a versatile enzyme that is able to use a broad spectrum of cofactors and cell precursors to initiate transcription, and that this ability is not restricted to NAD+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RNA polymerase is not a simple transcriptional machinery that is only able to transcribe DNA into RNA, but it can be used to produce a wide variety of molecules, such as RNAs, cell wall precursors or cofactors.
bacterial RNA polymerase is a promiscuous initiator of transcription with various nucleotide cofactors and cell surface precursors.

bacterial RNA polymerase is a highly versatile enzyme, capable of initiating transcription with a variety of adenosine- and uridine-containing factors, which may be involved in various cellular processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bacterial RNA polymerase can initiate transcription with various cofactors, including NAD+ and cell wall precursory factors.
RNA polymerase is capable of initiating transcription with a variety of cofactors and cell-wall precursors, and that this ability can be modulated by the σ factor.
the RNA polymerase of Escherichia coli is able to use a variety of adenosine- and uridine-containing cofactors to cap the 5′ ends of nascent RNA.
